concepts.title: The Ancestral Environment (EEA): The World Our Minds Were Built For
concepts.excerpt: The human mind was shaped by natural selection operating over millions of years in environments radically different from today's.

concepts.title: Behavioral Plasticity: How Fixed Programs Become Flexible Strategies
concepts.excerpt: Evolution's classic solution to environmental variation is genotype variation: different individuals with different genes survive better in different environments.

concepts.title: Frequency-Dependent Selection: Why Rare Strategies Can Be Successful
concepts.excerpt: Imagine a population of competing organisms. Some are aggressive (fight often, take risks), some are passive (avoid fights, conserve energy).

concepts.title: Costly Signaling
concepts.excerpt: This is counterintuitive. You'd think efficiency would be credible. But authenticity has always been costly.

concepts.title: Courtship Displays: Costly Signaling of Fitness and Commitment
concepts.excerpt: In mate competition, both sexes need credible signals: males must signal fitness (health, resources, genetic quality), females must signal fertility (age, health, reproductive capacity).

concepts.title: Male Expendability: The Evolutionary Gamble
concepts.excerpt: A female invests nine months of metabolic resources to produce one offspring.

concepts.title: Male-Female Strategic Asymmetry: Reproductive Gambit Differences
concepts.excerpt: Males and females face profoundly different reproductive constraints, and these constraints shape strategy at every level from individual behavior to civilizational organization.

concepts.title: Status Signaling: How Dominance and Wealth Are Displayed
concepts.excerpt: In animal hierarchies, dominance must be communicated so that subordinates can defer and avoid costly conflict.

concepts.title: Parental Investment Trade-Offs: The Allocation Problem Across Offspring and Time
concepts.excerpt: A parent has finite resources—time, energy, money, attention. These resources can be allocated across: (1) multiple offspring of different ages, (2) investment in current offspring vs.

concepts.title: Reproductive Value: The Age-Based Currency of Parental Investment
concepts.excerpt: Reproductive value is the expected number of offspring an individual will produce given their current age and condition.

concepts.title: Trivers-Willard Hypothesis: Sex-Biased Parental Investment Based on Parental Condition
concepts.excerpt: In environments where some males achieve much higher reproductive success than others (high variance), investment in sons produces higher return than investment in daughters—a son in good condition can father many offspring; a son in poor condition fathers few or none.

concepts.title: Serial Monogamy Effects: How Mating System Shifts Under Divorce Risk
concepts.excerpt: When monogamy is permanent and divorce unavailable, males face a straightforward calculation: invest in one female to secure her paternity confidence and reproductive capacity.

concepts.title: Non-Zero-Sum Cooperation: When 1+1>2
concepts.excerpt: Zero-sum games pit competitors against each other: your gain is my loss.

concepts.title: The Frontier Hypothesis: Expansion as Nervous System Health
concepts.excerpt: A superorganism with a frontier—unmapped territory, resources yet to be conquered, room to expand—is a superorganism in a state of optimism.

concepts.title: Gender Destruction as the Mechanism of Warrior-Making: How Institutions Create Killers
concepts.excerpt: Military training does not create warriors by teaching aggression. Aggression is already present in human beings.

concepts.title: Parental Investment Theory: The Reproductive Economy of Care
concepts.excerpt: Imagine two parents standing at the edge of reproductive possibility. One has already invested months of internal biological cost—gestation, nutrient transfer, hormonal upheaval—into a fetus.

concepts.title: Sexual Selection in Humans: The Architecture of Mate Competition
concepts.excerpt: Darwin observed peacocks with tails so elaborately maladapted to survival that they seemed to mock natural selection itself.
